messages:
Camille (Support): FYI customer acme-prod opened a high-priority ticket — p99 API latency jumped from ~80ms to 1.8s around 03:17 UTC. They say traffic should stay in EU. Trace shows an unexpected hop to AP-SOUTH. 
Netops Bot: :rotating_light: Alert: service=redwood-api cluster=eu-west-1 p99 latency sustained > 800ms for 6m (started 2025-03-07T03:17:12Z). Trace ID: trace-7f8a.
Camille (Support): @Elena @Ashok attaching the trace snippet the customer captured and their repro steps. They repro consistently by hitting our eu-west endpoint.
Camille (Support): ```
> trace-7f8a
client -> lb-eu-01 -> router-eu-az2 -> egress-proxy-02 (104.199.34.7) -> ap-south-1-edge (103.45.12.9) -> model-host-eu -> response
Duration: 1800ms (egress-proxy -> ap-south leg ~1200ms)
```
Ashok (Infra): Hmm — egress-proxy-02 forwarding to ap-south is the red flag. egress-proxy-02 should NAT to eu egress. Any recent routing policy changes?
Elena (SRE): Checking control plane events... I see a rollout at 03:12 UTC tagged "cost-aware-fallback-v3" that updated routing weights for egress regions. Could be related.
Ashok (Infra): That feature selects cheaper egress endpoint when under contention. If a weight calc bug used stale region-costs, it might prefer ap-south for some EU flows.
Camille (Support): Customer claims no config changes on their side. They included a curl they run: ```curl -v -H "Host: api.acme-prod" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/generate``` Repro is consistent for them.
Jamal (Customer): Confirmed — we ran the curl across 10 runs, 8/10 hit the slow path with ap-south hop, ~1.6–2.0s. Happened after ~03:15 UTC for us.
Elena (SRE): Can you paste the full control-plane change detail? I need the rollout id and the exact change.
Ashok (Infra): Rollout id: k8s-roll-20250307-0312 (cost-aware-fallback-v3). Diff shows: set egress-weight[ap-south]=0.6, egress-weight[eu-west]=0.4 for low-cost-fallback policy. Looks like the policy got applied globally instead of per-tenant.
Camille (Support): So ACME got hit by a global policy. Impact: cross-region hop -> extra ~1.2s.
Elena (SRE): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pin acme-prod to eu-west by inserting a per-tenant override (quick fix). 2) Roll back global rollout to previous weights. 3) Add tracepoints to egress-proxies to log chosen-policy and tenant id.
Ashok (Infra): I'm going to apply the tenant pin now (will route acme-prod via eu-west egress). Applying in 2m.
Netops Bot: Deploy started: pin-tenant-egress-acme-prod by Ashok — status: in_progress.
Camille (Support): Notifying customer that we're applying a pin and investigating root cause. Sending repro instructions to capture a network trace if it recurs.
Ashok (Infra): Pin applied. Netops Bot: Deploy succeeded. Can someone confirm p99 improved for the customer?
Jamal (Customer): Re-ran tests at 03:29 UTC — now p99 back to ~95ms for 10/10 runs. No more ap-south hop. Thanks.
Elena (SRE): Rolling back global rollout now and creating an emergency hotfix to scope the policy to traffic classes only (not global).
Camille (Support): Ticket update to customer: applied tenant pin and rolled back global weight change; monitoring.
Elena (SRE): Postmortem TODOs: (a) tight-scoping tests for cost-aware-fallback, (b) add per-tenant canary gating, (c) add metric that correlates region-change events with tenant IDs so support can triage faster.
Ashok (Infra): I'll push an instrumentation change to egress proxies to emit `egress_policy_id` and `selected_region` per request. That should make future traces self-describing.
Camille (Support): Thanks team. I'll close the customer loop and offer a credit for the window. Tagging @oncall for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
Elena (SRE): Filing incident-PR with timeline and the rollout diff.
Netops Bot: Incident created: INC-20250307-0317 — Severity: P2.
Camille (Support): Great. I'll attach logs and the customer's repro commands to the incident.
